Why fiberglass

Built in a factory. Set in weeks.

A one-piece Barrier Reef shell skips months of on-site construction and most of the long-term upkeep. Here's why that matters in Northeast Florida.

Weeks, not months

Barrier Reef puts a typical install at 2–6 weeks once permits clear, which matters in a Florida summer.

Smooth, non-porous gelcoat

The surface is gentle on feet and gives algae less to grip, so you typically use fewer chemicals.

No resurfacing, no liners

It avoids the biggest future bills of the other pool types: concrete resurfacing and vinyl liner replacement.

Compare fiberglass, concrete and vinyl →

Less scrubbing, more swimming.

  • Skim and keep the water balanced
  • Standard equipment servicing
  • Never drain the pool yourself: call us first

    Home/FAQ
    Fiberglass pool FAQ

    Straight answers, before you sign.

    What fiberglass pools cost in Jacksonville, how they compare with concrete and vinyl, and what it's really like to work with iTop Pools.

    Why fiberglassCost & financingFiberglass vs concrete vs vinylInstallation & permitsMaintenanceWarrantyWorking with iTop

    Why fiberglass

    Fiberglass is the fastest of the three to install, needs the least upkeep and rarely carries a big future repair bill, which is why many Jacksonville families choose it. The one-piece shell is made in a factory and set in weeks rather than months. Its smooth, non-porous gelcoat gives algae less to grip, so it typically needs fewer chemicals and less brushing. Concrete is the better answer when you need a truly custom shape, and vinyl usually has the lowest upfront price. See the full comparison guide.

    Yes, a fiberglass pool suits Northeast Florida when it is installed for the site's soil and groundwater. iTop Pools in Jacksonville checks access and soil on the site visit and plans the set around local conditions. One rule matters above all: never drain a fiberglass pool yourself, because high groundwater after heavy rain can push an empty shell upward. Before a storm, leave the pool full and follow the Pool School storm guidance.

    Fiberglass and concrete/gunite, plus paver decks, water features and outdoor kitchens. All built to take Florida sun, rain and daily use without looking tired in five years.

    Cost & financing

    A typical installed fiberglass pool runs about $58,000–$85,000, compared with about $78,000–$110,000 for concrete and about $40,000–$65,000 for vinyl liner. These are published ranges, before deck, enclosure and fencing, and they vary with size, site and features. iTop Pools gives you a firm written price after the site visit. Build your own estimate to see how the pieces add up.

    Get my firm price →

    Your total depends mostly on deck size and material, whether you add a screen enclosure, and how much access your yard allows. Florida also requires a pool safety feature, which is included in iTop's permitting plan. Because each yard differs, we measure first and then give you one written price covering the pool, deck, enclosure and permits. The estimator shows which choices move the number most.

    Get my firm price →

    Because we don't subcontract. Most builders hire out the shell, the deck and the pavers, and each layer adds its own markup. We have our own specialized crew for all of it, so you pay for the work instead of the middlemen.

    Most homeowners finance at least part of a pool, usually through an unsecured pool loan, a home equity loan, a HELOC or a cash-out refinance. Rates and terms depend on the lender and your credit, so talk to iTop about your options when we go through your price. Our financing guide compares all four in plain English.

    Get my firm price →

    Fiberglass vs concrete vs vinyl

    Fiberglass, concrete and vinyl liner pools compared
    CompareFiberglassConcrete (gunite)Vinyl liner
    Typical installed cost$58,000–$85,000$78,000–$110,000$40,000–$65,000
    Ownership cost, 10 yearsRoutine care only, in most casesRoutine care, plus higher chemical and cleaning needsRoutine care, plus possibly one liner ($3,000–$7,500)
    Ownership cost, 25 yearsRoutine care and equipment replacementOne or more resurfacings, priced by local quoteOften 2–3 liners ($6,000–$22,500 in total)
    Typical install time2–6 weeks after permits3–6 monthsSeveral weeks
    Maintenance and chemicalsLowestHighestMedium
    Surface feelSmooth gelcoatTextured plaster or pebbleSoft vinyl
    Algae resistanceHigh (non-porous)Lower (porous)Medium

    Published ranges for typical projects, before deck, enclosure and fencing. Vinyl figures are national because Florida figures were scarce. Ranges vary with size, site and features. iTop gives a firm written price after the site visit.

    Fiberglass usually has the lowest long-term ownership cost, because it avoids the two largest recurring bills: concrete resurfacing and vinyl liner replacement. Vinyl liners commonly need replacing every 10–15 years at about $3,000–$7,500 each, and Florida's sun can shorten that. Concrete needs periodic resurfacing and generally more chemicals. Actual costs depend on the pool and how it is cared for.

    Get my firm price →

    Concrete is the better choice when you want a vanishing edge, an unusual size or a shape no mold offers. Expect a longer build and periodic resurfacing over the pool's life. If your yard truly needs something custom, iTop will tell you so.

    Installation & permits

    Once permits and HOA approvals are finalized, Barrier Reef puts a typical fiberglass install at 2–6 weeks, depending on size, site and weather. Our crew isn't split across other companies' jobs, which is why we can move faster than most. You'll get a firm timeline before we break ground.

    Yes, and yes. HOA approvals, engineering and county permitting are all ours to chase, including the safety feature Florida law requires. You don't fill out a form or make a phone call.

    Our own crew: the same specialized team on every iTop job, for both pools and pavers. No rotating subcontractors, no one you haven't met and no finger-pointing when something needs fixing.

    Heavy rain can move a day here and there. We tell you when it happens instead of going quiet, and we keep the schedule moving around it.

    Maintenance

    A fiberglass pool needs less routine care than concrete or vinyl: mostly skimming, keeping the water balanced and standard equipment servicing. We build for low upkeep, and we walk you through exactly how to run it before we hand it over. Keep the water chemistry in range, because the finish warranty assumes it. Pool School has seasonal care guides written for Northeast Florida.

    Yes. Options like salt systems, variable-speed pumps and automation can cut running costs. We'll tell you which ones actually pay for themselves in your setup.

    Yes. Several Barrier Reef shells have a built-in lounging ledge or integrated spa, and separate spas, sundecks and tanning ledges can be added to many models. Heat pumps, salt systems, LED lighting and automation are also available. Filter the model finder by feature to see which shells include them.

    Warranty

    Barrier Reef provides a Lifetime Limited Structural Warranty on the shell, transferable once, plus a 15-year finish warranty against blistering. iTop separately warrants our installation work, and pumps, heaters and automation carry their own manufacturers' warranties. The written warranty documents govern. See who covers what.

    That's what the 3D design is for. We lay out size, shape, decking and finishes based on your yard and your budget, and you change anything you want while it's still free to change.

    Yes. Browse our work, or ask us and we'll arrange a visit to a finished project near you. We'd rather you stand next to the real thing.

    Process & warranty

    One crew. Zero hand-offs.

    Here's how a Barrier Reef shell gets from the factory to your backyard, who does each step, and exactly what's covered afterwards.

    Warranty, explained

    Two warranties. Both in writing.

    The manufacturer covers the shell. iTop covers the work. Here's who to call for what.

    Manufacturer · Barrier Reef

    The shell

    Lifetime Limited Structural Warranty

    The shell stays structurally sound, meaning capable of containing water, for the life of the pool. Transferable once if you sell your home.

    15-Year Finish Warranty

    Covers the gelcoat finish against blistering.

    Summary only. The written Barrier Reef warranty document governs, and it covers the pool shell only.

    Installer · iTop

    The workmanship

    Installation & plumbing

    Excavation, leveling, backfill, plumbing and equipment set by our own crew. Terms are set out in your written agreement.

    Decking & pavers

    Paver, travertine and porcelain decks laid by the same team. Terms are set out in your written agreement.

    Equipment

    Pumps, heaters and automation carry their manufacturers' warranties. We register them for you.

    You

    Keeping it valid

    Keep water balanced

    Finish warranties assume water chemistry stays in range. We show you how at handover.

    Never drain it yourself

    Groundwater can push an empty shell upward. Always call us first.

    Keep your paperwork

    We hand you the serial number, warranty registration and as-built drawing.
